title: Destiny 1 online protocol: BAP messages, investment replication, activity host (as emulated by d1-backend)

attrs.meaning: entity indices: 384-word bitmask granted to the client
instance state (0x6B0 bytes): valid flag, bubble count, bubble states, checksum, details with activity index / insertion point / scenario name
join result: identity echo (nonce must match), result 0
raw host event -> simulation event 0x13 (authority only)
membership update (present bit + struct): players, valid masks, host-tabulated region table
sync token (echoed in client 28); used as keep-alive

nodes.label: identity block {i32 nonce, u64 host id, {machine[8], player[8], account, character, fireteam}, properties 0x80800B1F, ...}
player properties {i8, session id string, i64 x4 (fireteam id @0xA0 in the slot), i32 x2, machine[8]}
instance details (0x650, at instance +0x60): activity index @+0x5C0, insertion point @+0x5C2, scenario name char[40] @+0x5C8 (instance +0x620/+0x622/+0x628)
activity membership (0x5038): u32 x2, players[20] x 0x250, region table @0x2E48, masks @0x5028/0x502C/0x5030
debug update {count, 512 x 16 bytes} + raw bytes
character flag slot 673 (must be true for the prologue)
Cosmodrome ambient activity tag (class 0x80800861) registered as client reference type 0x10 during the prologue; byte +0x1AC = -1
BAP message that delivers activity-host messages to the client (answer: bap_to_client_notification 9)
host message that feeds the client's simulation queue
type of the 1608-byte second blob of the host-startup request

assertions.claim: BAP message ids and header classes come from vtable slots 0 and 1 of each c_investment_bap_message_* class; push_policy_* objects pick the handler for received messages, policy_* objects map send kinds to message types.

Host -> client activity messages arrive as bap_to_client_notification (9) with payload [1][u64 BE host id][u32 BE type][u32 BE len][data]; activity_host_to_client_notification (100) is only relayed by the client to the BAP service named in its header (push policy 0x565DB0).
Client -> host activity messages are client_to_activity_host_notification (8): header class 3 (base + u64 BE target host id), payload [1][u32 BE type][u32 BE len][u32 0][data] (0x55FD50).

Activity-host payloads are engine-type bitstreams (MSB first, value + bias in n bits, presence bits for optional members); type descriptors were dumped from the running client (backend/data/investment_schema.json).
Investment objects replicate in families (object manager slots); updates use the queuez format (u32 BE count, per family {type, root, version, flags, n, objects}).
Flag 836 must be false and 2838 true for the new-character prologue; the prologue's purchase prerequisite is f[0x1A3] || f[0x1B8] (scope-0 flags, set through the profile override list).

Activity index 164 (hash 0x6E0DAE89, the new-character prologue) loads scenario act_cosmo_m0_highway: checksum 0x8FE07299 (tag data +0xC), 22 bubbles (tag data +0x48); initial region PRV00.00 (hash 0x555CCDF4) is slot 0.

sources.locator: eboot.bin 01.33 (sha256 672f0341...0833): c_investment_bap_message_* vtables, slot 0 = message id, slot 1 = header class
d1-native + d1-backend headless runs n30-n55 and gdb probes, 2026-10-13 (logs not committed)

rejections.reason: The client's push policy for 100 relays it back out to the service named in its header; nothing reaches the activity client.
0x29DE50 decodes the update and discards it.
Decoding it as the instance details consumes only ~540 of 12864 bits at any alignment.

frontiers.question: What registers the current activity's mode reference (client reference type 0x10) so that its +0x1AC byte is positive for the prologue? Loading task 9 (0x7965A0) waits for it; D1_BYPASS=spawn skips it.
